/*
  Seam between Angular Material (M3 system tokens) and Tailwind: --mat-sys-* -> Tailwind theme namespaces.
  Colors keep M3 role names (--mat-sys-on-primary -> text-on-primary); scales use Tailwind sizes (large -> lg, extra-small -> xs).
  Values come from mat.theme() in material-theme.scss; light/dark is resolved by color-scheme, not by this file.
  Only semantic roles are mapped; Material does not expose its tonal palettes as variables.
  Overlaps tokens.css (surface, on-surface) and tailwindcss-primeui (primary): import one seam, not both.
  Wiring: @import './design/material-tokens.css'; after tailwindcss in styles.css.
*/

The repeated sets are extracted with `@apply` into `@layer components` in `src/styles.css#L13-L60`: `btn-filled`, `btn-outlined`, `btn-text`, `field`, `card`, `meta`, `list-item`, `list-item-active`, `badge`, and `task-row`. Things that changed beyond a pure color swap, so you can check them:
- Font weights now come from the M3 type roles (`text-title-sm`, `text-label-md`, and so on), so the `font-semibold` and `font-bold` classes are gone and headings render at M3 weights.
- Status badges map to M3 container roles: negotiation and medium use tertiary, new uses secondary, proposal uses surface-variant, and closed-lost and high use error.
- Rounded corners follow the token scale (`rounded-sm`, `rounded-md`, `rounded-xs`).
- Hover states use `primary/90` and the container roles, not state-layer opacities.

_**Agent (copilot/claude-haiku-5.5)**_

Most interactive and structural elements in `src/app/deals-page/deals-page.ts` have a direct Angular Material equivalent:

| Current element | Material replacement |
|---|---|
| `New Deal`, `Add` buttons | `button[matButton="filled"]` |
| `Edit` button | `button[matButton="outlined"]` |
| `Archive completed` link-style button | `button[matButton="text"]` |
| Filter search input and its SVG icon | `mat-form-field` with `matInput`, plus `mat-icon` as `matSuffix` (`search` ligature) |
| `New task` input | `mat-form-field` with `matInput` and a `mat-label` |
| `Priority` select | `mat-form-field` with `mat-select` and `mat-option` |
| Task checkboxes | `mat-checkbox` |
| Status and priority badges (`negotiation`, `new`, `high`, etc.) | `mat-chip` inside `mat-chip-set` |
| Deal list in the aside | `mat-nav-list` with `a[mat-list-item]`, or `mat-selection-list` for single selection |
| Task list | `mat-list` with `mat-list-item` |
| Deal and Tasks `section` panels | `mat-card` with `mat-card-header`, `mat-card-title`, `mat-card-content` |
| Header bar | `mat-toolbar` |
| Dividers, if added | `mat-divider` |

Elements with no direct Material component, which stay as plain HTML with the existing layout classes:
- The page grid (`grid grid-cols-[260px_1fr]`). A `mat-drawer` layout is possible but heavier than this static aside needs.
- The `dl` / `dt` / `dd` field summary. `mat-card-content` can hold it, but no component models it.
- Headings and body text, which use the typography tokens.

Using these components means adding their modules or standalone imports to the component's `imports` array, which is a TypeScript change. Your earlier request said template only, so I'd need your go-ahead to touch the component class.

- **Task rows:** `mat-list-item` with `mat-checkbox`. The completed task keeps its line-through.
- **Badges:** `mat-chip` inside `mat-chip-set`.

Changes you might not expect:
- The Edit and Archive buttons moved from the top of their panels to `mat-card-actions` at the bottom.
- The chips use Material's default styling, so the old status colors (negotiation, new, high, and so on) are gone.
- In `styles.css` I removed the now-unused `.btn-*`, `.field`, `.card`, `.list-item*`, `.badge`, and `.task-row` classes. I kept `.meta` because the deal details still use it.

Here are proposed fixes for the two issues. I haven't changed any files.

**1. Deal names truncate in the left list ("Enterprise L…")**

The aside is a fixed `260px` column (`grid-cols-[260px_1fr]`). The title shares that width with the status chip in the meta slot, so the title is cut off.

- Recommended: widen the column to `grid-cols-[300px_1fr]` in the main grid. Add a `title` attribute on each title span so the full name is still available on hover.
- Alternative: keep the width and move the status chip under the amount line, out of the meta slot. This frees horizontal space for the title.

**2. Priority chip sits above its task row in the Tasks list**

Material places `matListItemMeta` at the top of a multi-line list item. The chip lines up with the title, not with the item's center, so the row looks uneven next to the checkbox and due date.

- Recommended: add `class="self-center"` to each task's `mat-chip-set matListItemMeta`, then verify with a screenshot. I haven't confirmed that this class takes effect inside the Material list item, so I'd check the result before calling it fixed.
- Alternative: move the chip into the `matListItemLine` slot next to "Due: …". This keeps every row on two lines with one consistent layout.

Your `mat-chip-set { display: flex !important; }` rule in `deals-page.ts` may also affect chip alignment. I'd keep it for now and remove it only if the fixes above make it unnecessary.

## Project practices from this chat

**Angular conventions (from `AGENTS.md`)**
- Use standalone components. Don't set `standalone: true` (default in v20+).
- Don't set `changeDetection: OnPush` explicitly (default in v22+).
- Use signals for state. Use `input()`, `output()`, `model()` for two-way binding, `computed()` for derived state, and `linkedSignal()` for synchronized derived state.
- Use `update()` or `set()` on signals, never `mutate()`.
- Use native control flow (`@if`, `@for`, `@switch`). Don't use `*ngIf`, `*ngFor`, `ngClass`, `ngStyle`, or `CommonModule`.
- Use `inject()`, not constructor injection. Use `@Service` for singletons (v22+).
- Put host bindings in the `host` object, not `@HostBinding` or `@HostListener`.
- Use `NgOptimizedImage` for static images, but not for inline base64.
- Prefer Signal Forms for new forms. Otherwise use reactive forms, not template-driven.
- Lazy-load feature routes. Keep components small and inline templates for small ones.
- Use strict TypeScript, prefer inference, and avoid `any` (use `unknown`).
- Meet AXE checks and WCAG AA, including focus, contrast, and ARIA.

**Styling decisions**
- Map `--mat-sys-*` roles to Tailwind namespaces with `@theme inline` in `material-tokens.css`. Use semantic classes such as `bg-surface` and `text-on-surface`, not raw palette classes.
- Extract repeated class sets with `@apply` inside `@layer components` in `styles.css`.
- Tailwind utilities override `@layer components` classes. For example, `pr-9` overrode `.field` padding.
- Remove CSS classes once the markup that used them is gone.
- The editor's CSS linter reports `@theme` and `@apply` as errors. These are false positives.

**Angular Material decisions**
- Use `button[matButton="filled|outlined|text|tonal|elevated"]`, not the old `mat-raised-button` style.
- Verify selectors and inputs against the installed package (`fesm2022`) rather than guessing. Material 22.2.5 is installed.
- Import each Material component in the standalone  array.
- `mat-icon` ligatures need the Material Symbols font. `index.html` already loads it.
- Use `mat-list-item` with `button` and `[activated]`, `mat-card appearance="outlined"`, `mat-chip-set`, and `mat-form-field` with `mat-label`.

**Workflow and tooling**
- Format with prettier (`.prettierrc`: `printWidth` 100, `singleQuote`, Angular parser for HTML). Run `--check` or `--write` on changed files only.
- Type-check with `npx tsc --noEmit -p tsconfig.app.json`.
- Add ESLint with `ng add angular-eslint`, then lint changed files only.
- Prefer the running `ng serve` over `ng build`. Confirm before using browser tools.

# Angular Rules

## TypeScript Best Practices

- Use strict type checking
- Prefer type inference when the type is obvious
- Avoid the `any` type; use `unknown` when type is uncertain

## Angular Best Practices

- Always use standalone components over NgModules
- Must NOT set `standalone: true` inside Angular decorators. It's the default in Angular v20+.
- Do NOT set `changeDetection: ChangeDetectionStrategy.OnPush` explicitly. `OnPush` is the default in Angular v22+.
- Use signals for state management
- Implement lazy loading for feature routes
- Do NOT use the `@HostBinding` and `@HostListener` decorators. Put host bindings inside the `host` object of the `@Component` or `@Directive` decorator instead
- Use `NgOptimizedImage` for all static images.
  - `NgOptimizedImage` does not work for inline base64 images.

## Accessibility Requirements

- It MUST pass all AXE checks.
- It MUST follow all WCAG AA minimums, including focus management, color contrast, and ARIA attributes.

## Components

- Keep components small and focused on a single responsibility
- Use `input()` and `output()` functions instead of decorators
- Use `model()` for two-way bound properties with `[(prop)]` syntax instead of pairing `input()` with `output()`
- Use `computed()` for derived state
- Use `linkedSignal()` for state derived from multiple reactive sources that must stay synchronized
- Prefer inline templates for small components
- Prefer Signal Forms (`@angular/forms/signals`) for new forms. They are stable in Angular v22+ and provide signal-based state, type-safe field access, and schema-based validation
- When not using Signal Forms, prefer Reactive forms instead of Template-driven ones
- Do NOT use `ngClass`, use `class` bindings instead
- Do NOT use `ngStyle`, use `style` bindings instead
- Do NOT import `CommonModule`, import only the directives and pipes the template uses, such as `AsyncPipe` or `DatePipe`
- When using external templates/styles, use paths relative to the component TS file.

## State Management

- Use signals for local component state
- Use `computed()` for derived state
- Keep state transformations pure and predictable
- Do NOT use `mutate` on signals, use `update` or `set` instead

## Templates

- Keep templates simple and avoid complex logic
- Use native control flow (`@if`, `@for`, `@switch`) instead of `*ngIf`, `*ngFor`, `*ngSwitch`
- Use the async pipe to handle observables
- Do not assume globals like (`new Date()`) are available.

## Services

- Design services around a single responsibility
- Use the `providedIn: 'root'` option for singleton services
- Prefer the `@Service` decorator over `@Injectable({providedIn: 'root'})` for new singleton services (Angular v22+)
- Use the `inject()` function instead of constructor injection

## Angular Material

- Import Material components through the arrays exported from `src/app/shared/shared-module.ts` (`SharedForms`, `SharedUI`). Spread them into the component `imports` array, for example `imports: [...SharedUI]`.
- Add any new Material component to those arrays before using it in a template.
- Use `button[matButton="filled|outlined|text|tonal|elevated"]`, not the old `mat-raised-button`-style attributes.
- Verify Material selectors and inputs against `node_modules/@angular/material` before use.

## Styling

- Use semantic classes such as `bg-surface` and `text-on-surface`, not raw palette classes.
- Extract class sets repeated across multiple components with `@apply` inside `@layer components`.
- Tailwind utilities override `@layer components` classes. Check for utility conflicts, for example `pr-9` overrode `.field` padding.
- Remove CSS classes once no markup uses them.
- Avoid `::ng-deep` and `!important`. Prefer CSS variables and tokens. If an override is unavoidable, use a named class such as `.fix-<name>-override`.

# Angular Rules

## TypeScript Best Practices

- Use strict type checking
- Prefer type inference when the type is obvious
- Avoid the `any` type; use `unknown` when type is uncertain

## Angular Best Practices

- Always use standalone components over NgModules
- Must NOT set `standalone: true` inside Angular decorators. It's the default in Angular v20+.
- Do NOT set `changeDetection: ChangeDetectionStrategy.OnPush` explicitly. `OnPush` is the default in Angular v22+.
- Use signals for state management
- Implement lazy loading for feature routes
- Do NOT use the `@HostBinding` and `@HostListener` decorators. Put host bindings inside the `host` object of the `@Component` or `@Directive` decorator instead
- Use `NgOptimizedImage` for all static images.
  - `NgOptimizedImage` does not work for inline base64 images.

## Accessibility Requirements

- It MUST pass all AXE checks.
- It MUST follow all WCAG AA minimums, including focus management, color contrast, and ARIA attributes.

## Components

- Keep components small and focused on a single responsibility
- Use `input()` and `output()` functions instead of decorators
- Use `model()` for two-way bound properties with `[(prop)]` syntax instead of pairing `input()` with `output()`
- Use `computed()` for derived state
- Use `linkedSignal()` for state derived from multiple reactive sources that must stay synchronized
- Prefer inline templates for small components
- Prefer Signal Forms (`@angular/forms/signals`) for new forms. They are stable in Angular v22+ and provide signal-based state, type-safe field access, and schema-based validation
- When not using Signal Forms, prefer Reactive forms instead of Template-driven ones
- Do NOT use `ngClass`, use `class` bindings instead
- Do NOT use `ngStyle`, use `style` bindings instead
- Do NOT import `CommonModule`, import only the directives and pipes the template uses, such as `AsyncPipe` or `DatePipe`
- When using external templates/styles, use paths relative to the component TS file.

## State Management

- Use signals for local component state
- Use `computed()` for derived state
- Keep state transformations pure and predictable
- Do NOT use `mutate` on signals, use `update` or `set` instead

## Templates

- Keep templates simple and avoid complex logic
- Use native control flow (`@if`, `@for`, `@switch`) instead of `*ngIf`, `*ngFor`, `*ngSwitch`
- Use the async pipe to handle observables
- Do not assume globals like (`new Date()`) are available.

## Services

- Design services around a single responsibility
- Use the `providedIn: 'root'` option for singleton services
- Prefer the `@Service` decorator over `@Injectable({providedIn: 'root'})` for new singleton services (Angular v22+)
- Use the `inject()` function instead of constructor injection

## Angular Material

- Import Material components through the arrays exported from `src/app/shared/shared-module.ts` (`SharedForms`, `SharedUI`). Spread them into the component `imports` array, for example `imports: [...SharedUI]`.
- Add any new Material component to those arrays before using it in a template.
- Use `button[matButton="filled|outlined|text|tonal|elevated"]`, not the old `mat-raised-button`-style attributes.
- Verify Material selectors and inputs against `node_modules/@angular/material` before use.

## Styling

- Use semantic classes such as `bg-surface` and `text-on-surface`, not raw palette classes.
- Extract class sets repeated across multiple components with `@apply` inside `@layer components`.
- Tailwind utilities override `@layer components` classes. Check for utility conflicts, for example `pr-9` overrode `.field` padding.
- Remove CSS classes once no markup uses them.
- Avoid `::ng-deep` and `!important`. Prefer CSS variables and tokens. If an override is unavoidable, use a named class such as `.fix-<name>-override`.
